rollback_rehearsal.action: AGENTIHOOKS_RUNTIME_DISABLED=<backend> in the swarm tick environment routes new spawns to the local adapter; existing attempt records keep their runtime_backend and their operations return unavailable
rollback_rehearsal.case: c: a disabled remote left its attempt record and runtime object unchanged, a new spawn went local, and after re-enabling a replayed spawn reached only the owning remote, which returned the first object without a duplicate

remaining_limitations: Replay deduplication is the owning backend's: the router forwards a replayed spawn to its owner and adds no second backend; reconciliation by immutable execution ID (INV-R06) and generation fencing (INV-R07) are not implemented here.
The T-SV2-RUN-01-C ownership assertion (a stale attempt cannot overwrite a newer accepted result) is not tested here: there are no generations at this layer yet; it is deferred with INV-R07.

Every lifecycle call from the tick and the swarm CLI (spawn, observe, command, retire, reattach, resume, snapshot restore) goes through RuntimeRouter. HerdrRuntime still answers directly for live names, bindings, refusals, status and conversations, and for the local pane and process actions reap_name, name_pane and close_space, which key on names rather than runtime objects; moving those under the owner check belongs with SV2-RUN-02.
No remote backend exists yet; the remote runtime is a fixture.
runtime_capability_failures_total is an in-process counter on RuntimeRouter with no exporter.
No live rollout proof; the evidence is a local isolated fixture plus CI.
